A model used in the public health system, private hospitals, remote monitoring programs, or genetic cardiology clinics should be tested in the populations and workflows where it will influence decisions.
Training should teach users not only what the model predicts, but what data it uses, what it omits, how it fails, how uncertainty is displayed, when to override it, and how to document disagreement.

Interfaces should make uncertainty visible rather than hiding it behind polished dashboards.
When it does not, clinicians must be able to override it, document the reasoning, and learn from the discrepancy.

Before deployment, institutions should specify who receives the output, who must acknowledge it, what action is expected, when escalation is required, how disagreement is documented, how overrides are reviewed, and when the model should be paused or retired.
Institutions should treat AI deployment as a clinical governance responsibility.
A risk score without a plausible action pathway is often an information burden rather than a cognitive aid.
Each group interacts with AI at a different point in the cognitive chain and therefore needs different explanations, thresholds, training, and governance.

The output should specify what was detected or predicted, which data drove the result, what important data were missing, how uncertain the estimate is, whether the patient resembles the validation population, what actions may reasonably follow, and what actions should not follow.
Equity requires more than fairness metrics after deployment.

unlisted_practices: Communicate AI results to patients and families in understandable terms, including what the result means, what it does not mean, and how it will influence the next decision.
Design AI systems to create appropriate friction at moments of uncertainty, mismatch, or high consequence.
Evaluate cardiovascular AI as a clinical-cognitive intervention across technical, clinical, cognitive, workflow, equity, and lifecycle validity, not technical metrics alone.
Pair institutional endorsement of AI tools with local performance monitoring and clear escalation rules.
